renames.NLAlib/Matrix/Norms.lean: NLAlib/Matrix/Norms.lean is reserved for the generated aggregator; it holds the leaf's definitions (frobInner, frobSq, frobNorm, specNorm), so it becomes Norms/Basic.lean.
renames.NLAlib/Matrix/Spectral.lean: NLAlib/Matrix/Spectral.lean is reserved for the generated aggregator; it holds the leaf's core definitions (lamMin, sigmaMin, sigmaMinSq), so it becomes Spectral/Basic.lean.

notes: Factorizations/ moved wholesale with unchanged names (Cholesky, Givens, GramSchmidt, Hessenberg, Householder, LU, QR, Triangular).

The codex Gram soft-min / inverse-power / cutoff calculus family moves together to Matrix/Structured (GramSoftMin, GramSoftMinSpectral, GramSoftMinMeasurable, GramCutoffCalculus, UnshiftedGramSoftMin, InversePowerConcavity, InversePowerGrowth, InversePowerLimit, InversePowerLaplacianLimit, GramTrace). Its generic helpers go by topic instead: InverseCalculus (derivative of the matrix inverse and trace powers) and CFCTrace go to Functions, CoordinateUpdates (a one-lemma matrix-unit identity) goes to Basic, SpectralMinimum goes to Spectral and SpectralContinuity goes to Perturbation.

Real and complex twins share a directory: EckartYoung/ComplexEckartYoung/ComplexGramTruncation/ComplexBestRankApproximation are in Spectral; the complex column projectors (ComplexVolumeProjection, ComplexProjectionBounds, ComplexProjectionComposition, ComplexVolumeProjectorTrace) are in Subspaces next to Projections; TraceTail/ComplexTraceTail are in Inequalities; DiagonalFilter/ComplexDiagonalFilter are in Functions; GramColumnDeterminant/ComplexGramColumnDeterminant are in Subspaces.

Pseudoinverses (Pseudoinverse, MoorePenrose, SingletonInverse, ComplexFullRowInverse) and LeastSquares go to Basic as foundational definitions. LeastSquares sensitivity is in Conditioning, which goes to Perturbation.

SchurComplement goes to Basic, not Inequalities: 12 of its 22 declarations are the pivotSchur elimination step and bordered-matrix identities that Factorizations/LU and LowRank/PartialCholesky import. Albert's criterion and its Loewner corollaries are the minority (see flags).

Within Matrix/ only the measurability lemmas that are entrywise (Measurable, SpectralMeasurable, GramSoftMinMeasurable, PolarFrame, OptimalErrorContinuity) stay, following STANDARDS §3 ('a measurability fact about matrices in Matrix/Measurable.lean'). They import Mathlib measure theory but no NLAlib probability and declare no instances. Files that declare Borel/MeasurableSpace instances (Stiefel) or depend on them (CanonicalQR) leave for RandomMatrix/Haar.

Import check: no M1 file imports anything from Concentration, Gaussian, Sketching, Krylov, Polynomial, LowRank, Estimation or Solvers today. The only cross-tree destinations, RandomMatrix/Haar/{Stiefel,CanonicalQR}, are imported only by Gaussian/HaarFrameMeasure and Gaussian/HaarQR, which M3 sends to RandomMatrix/Haar.

Coordination with M2: CoordinatePinching (Golden–Thompson pinching helpers, imported only by Concentration/Matrix/OperatorConvexity/GoldenThompson) goes to Matrix/OperatorTheory, assuming M2 places OperatorConvexity there. If M2 keeps GoldenThompson in Probability/Concentration/Matrix, CoordinatePinching can still stay (layer 0 is below 1).

Coordinator: the Gram soft-min / inverse-power calculus family moved to the new leaf Matrix/Calculus: GramCutoffCalculus.lean, GramSoftMin.lean, GramSoftMinSpectral.lean, GramTrace.lean, InversePowerConcavity.lean, InversePowerGrowth.lean, InversePowerLaplacianLimit.lean, InversePowerLimit.lean, UnshiftedGramSoftMin.lean
flags: NLAlib/Matrix/Stiefel.lean: the brief lists Stiefel under Matrix/Subspaces, but the file declares orthogonalGroupMeasurableSpace/orthogonalGroupBorelSpace instances and imports MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.Basic. The Borel-instance rule excludes it from Matrix/, so it goes to RandomMatrix/Haar (its only external importer is Gaussian/HaarFrameMeasure). Alternative: Matrix/Subspaces, if Borel instances on the orthogonal group are acceptable at layer 0.

NLAlib/Matrix/CanonicalQR.lean: a canonical positive-diagonal thin QR built as a Borel map into Stiefel space. It imports Stiefel and Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace, so it follows Stiefel to RandomMatrix/Haar (its only importer is Gaussian/HaarQR). Alternative: Matrix/Factorizations next to QR if Stiefel stays in Matrix. It mixes the QR algebra with measurability; split later (the algebraic QR half belongs in Factorizations).

NLAlib/Matrix/Measurable.lean, SpectralMeasurable.lean, GramSoftMinMeasurable.lean: placed in Matrix/Structured as the brief asks ('measurability files if they are matrix-only'). They import Mathlib BorelSpace/MeasureTheory, which the layer sentence of the brief literally disqualifies; the two instructions conflict. Their importers are all at layer >= 1 (Gaussian/*, LowRank/*), so Probability/Basic is a layer-safe alternative if Matrix/ should be measure-free. Structured is a poor topical name for them (see missing directories).

NLAlib/Matrix/PolarFrame.lean: mixes the polar orthonormal frame Y(YᵀY)^{-1/2} (Subspaces) with its entrywise measurability (imports Matrix.Measurable). Mapped to Subspaces per the brief; split the measurability lemmas later.

NLAlib/Matrix/OptimalErrorContinuity.lean: mostly Lipschitz continuity of the best-rank Frobenius error (Perturbation), plus one measurable_bestRankFrobSq lemma that imports BorelSpace.Basic. Mapped to Perturbation; split the measurable lemma later.

NLAlib/Matrix/SchurComplement.lean: mixes the pivotSchur elimination step (Basic/Factorizations) with Albert's criterion and Schur-complement Loewner bounds (Inequalities). Mapped to Basic; split later, with the Albert/Loewner half going to Inequalities.

NLAlib/Matrix/SpectralBounds.lean: mixes spectral-norm perturbation of sigmaMin (3 declarations, atlas norm-lipschitz) with foundational singular-value identities (singularValues_zero_eq_specNorm, sigmaMin_eq_singularValues_last, orthonormal-column specNorm identities) that EckartYoung, PolynomialCalculus and RankNorm import. Mapped to Spectral; split the perturbation lemmas into Perturbation later.

NLAlib/Matrix/FiniteIndexTransport.lean: reindexing transport for norms, rank, Moore–Penrose, singular values and the best-rank optimum. It touches several topics; mapped to Spectral (dominant: best-rank / singular values).

NLAlib/Matrix/PowerRayleigh.lean: the deterministic power-method Rayleigh/log-overlap bound, imported by Krylov/MeasurableRitz and LowRank/RandomStartPower. Mapped to Matrix/Spectral; Krylov/Spectral (next to PowerMethod) is a layer-safe alternative if M5 prefers.

NLAlib/Matrix/GramSingularBounds.lean and ComplexEmbedding.lean: Gram-error to singular-value or norm-preservation bounds (deterministic steps of the subspace-embedding proofs). Mapped to Perturbation; Spectral would also be defensible.

NLAlib/Matrix/Walsh.lean, WalshFin.lean: Walsh–Hadamard matrices are 'structured matrices' in the usual sense, so they go to Matrix/Structured. That puts them next to the unrelated Gram soft-min calculus family, which this directory also holds per the brief.
